title: Default and Reinstatement of a Patient Payment Plan
content:
**Credit and Collections policy — default notice, default and reinstatement of a Patient Payment Plan**

### 1. Default notice
When the count of consecutive missed installments reaches the tier's figure for missed installments to default, a default notice is sent. Consecutive missed installments are the installments of the plan recorded as missed whose due dates fall after the latest installment paid in full, or after signing where no installment has yet been paid in full.

### 2. Default
A plan defaults no earlier than the tier's default-notice period, in calendar days, after the date the default notice was sent, and only if it is still past due. Days are counted as calendar days from the notice date, the notice date itself being day zero. The notice date is the date of the default notice entry on that plan's history.

### 3. Effect of default
On default, where the tier returns a defaulted plan's balance to statements, the remaining balance returns to the plans of care it came from and resumes the regular statement cycle.

### 4. Reinstatement
Where the tier allows reinstatement, a defaulted plan is reinstated only no later than the tier's reinstatement window, in calendar days, after the default date on file, once every missed installment is paid, and at most the tier's limit of reinstatements per plan. The returned balance is moved back into the plan. Days for reinstatement are counted as calendar days from the default date, the default date itself being day zero. The default date is the one recorded on that plan.

## Clock summary

| Gate | Starts from | Comparison | Boundary day |
|---|---|---|---|
| Default (section 2) | Date the default notice was sent (day zero) | Not earlier than the notice period | The day the count reaches the period is included |
| Reinstatement (section 4) | Default date on file (day zero) | Not later than the reinstatement window | The day the count reaches the window is included |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates and periods)

- **Default, 10-day notice period.** Notice sent 2026-06-02. On 2026-06-11 (day 9) the plan does not default. From 2026-06-12 (day 10) it may default, provided it is still past due; a plan brought current before then does not default.
- **Reinstatement, 30-day window.** Default date 2026-07-01. On 2026-07-31 (day 30) the plan may still be reinstated, once every missed installment is paid and within the reinstatement limit. On 2026-08-01 (day 31) it is outside the window.
- **Consecutive count.** A plan's latest installment paid in full was due 2026-02-15; installments due 2026-03-15 and 2026-04-15 are recorded as missed. The consecutive count is 2. On a tier whose figure is 2, the default notice is sent; on a tier whose figure is 3, it is not yet sent.
